summary:
Amasya stands under the national framework of Türkiye. The source inventory records no Amasya-specific provision, ordinance, enforcement finding or incident; what a trans visitor faces in the province is the country-wide regime, applied without documented local mitigation or local aggravation.

A leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package', reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025, would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people. Human Rights Watch described it as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades. Conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', including its so-called 'promotion', would carry up to three years in prison, and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies up to four years; same-sex marriage is not legal in Türkiye, so such ceremonies are by definition symbolic. Gender-affirming care would be restricted under the package: the surgery age raised from 18 to 25, permanent infertility made a precondition, medical professionals fined or imprisoned for up to seven years for care outside the new limits, and transgender patients facing up to three years — a set of provisions that would push treatment into underground settings. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's 2025 report, 'A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy', documents six right-to-life violations over the year, three recorded as hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected. Türkiye keeps no official hate-crime statistics, so these counts are drawn from media and civil-society reports rather than state records. The report also records 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the previous year, mostly linked to peaceful assembly, alongside 336 assembly violations and 313 liberty violations — a roughly 2.5-fold rise in liberty violations consisting mostly of detentions — together with event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings.

The hostility documented in the report is institutionalised through 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events, applied as country-wide practice rather than provincial choice. The report contains no Amasya-specific finding.
tangentialFactors:
The 2025 counts in the Kaos GL report are raw totals for the whole country, drawn from media and civil-society monitoring because Türkiye maintains no official hate-crime statistics. Raw counts track population and monitoring capacity, so they cannot be read as a per-capita danger ranking for any one province, and Amasya's absence from the report reflects the absence of a documented local case rather than a demonstrated local safety record.

The draft '11th Judicial Package' sits within a broader pattern of state framing — 'Year of the Family' instructions, official hate speech, censored broadcasts — rather than an isolated legislative move, which matters for how a visitor reads local official attitudes in Amasya even where no provincial directive is on record.
localsOnly:
Residents of Amasya live under the same national framework described for visitors: the draft package's restrictions on gender-affirming care, including the raised surgery age and infertility precondition, would bind local medical providers and patients directly, with professional penalties of up to seven years and patient penalties of up to three years for care outside the new limits.

Local LGBTI+ residents are also subject to the assembly and liberty violations catalogued nationally — detentions, event bans and police action against gatherings — with no Amasya-specific exemption or local protective policy recorded in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the '11th Judicial Package' has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 Human Rights Watch report is unresolved in the sources.

No source in the inventory addresses Amasya's own municipal ordinances, local police practice, or provincial health facilities for trans residents; the absence of a local finding is an absence of monitoring, not a verified absence of risk.

The Kaos GL counts rest on media and civil-society monitoring because no official hate-crime statistics exist, so provincial distribution of the documented violations cannot be resolved from these sources.
